clue.text: Striking example of an evil personality

definitions.meaning: an old name for a friction match, something struck to light it
the name of the fallen angel, Satan

explanation.surface: Someone notable is held up as a shining instance of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an old-fashioned match struck to light; the other is the devil's name before his fall.

clue.text: Audible fault in circuitry

indicators.note: audible means the word is heard rather than seen, so we want something sounding like it

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or fault

explanation.surface: A humming noise reveals a defect in some electrical wiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuitry' is read as circuits of a racetrack, not electrical wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Laps are complete circuits of a track, so the plural stands for circuits run.

clue.text: I leave head cook in charge

indicators.note: leave tells us the letter I departs from the word for head

parts.note: a chief is a head or leader

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are quitting as the senior cook in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for chief, it names the head cook running a kitchen.

clue.text: A way of drawing liberal applause

parts.note: liberal in the sense of open, unrestricted, free
to give someone a hand is to applaud them

explanation.surface: An artist's method is said to win generous clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing done without rulers or tracing is called freehand sketching.

clue.text: Tees, say, first stolen from golf club

indicators.note: the opening letter is taken away from the word for a golf club

parts.note: a driver is a golf club used for tee shots

explanation.surface: Golf tees go missing from a club, a picture of theft on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tees' looks like golf pegs beside 'golf club'; it is the river Tees in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is an English waterway, given as an example of the class.

clue.text: Two bills I stuck on a tree

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a second account, abbreviated AC again

explanation.surface: Someone pins a pair of invoices to a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck on' just joins the pieces, placing A after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a thorny tree or shrub, the wattle of Australia.

clue.text: People will mind if you dump your kids here

definitions.text: People will mind if you dump your kids here

parts.words: People will mind if you dump your kids here
parts.note: read 'mind' not as object but as look after: a place where staff care for children left there

explanation.definitionFit: A daytime nursery where young children are looked after while parents work.

clue.text: Company moderating our panic, providing a huge supply

indicators.note: moderating suggests toning down and so reworking the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A firm calms everyone's alarm by promising plenty of stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moderating' reads as calming the panic, but it is the signal to rework the letters; 'providing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The horn of plenty is a symbol of abundance, hence any overflowing supply.

clue.text: Rise secures unemployment benefit for a youngster

indicators.note: secures means holds inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or climb
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A pay rise wins jobless money for a young person.
explanation.walkthrough: THE DOLE is everyday British slang for state unemployment pay; 'secures' means it is held within the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager between childhood and adulthood, a young person.

clue.text: Pickle, perhaps, specially for game

definitions.meaning: jam, chutney or pickle are kinds of ... food
land kept specially for game animals to be bred and hunted

explanation.surface: A jar of chutney is made specially for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserved food such as jam, and also a reserve of land kept for game.

clue.text: Word that is coined for an eccentric

indicators.note: a coined word is newly made up, so these letters are minted afresh

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone has invented a new term for an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun for a strange or odd person, an oddball.

clue.text: Harsh cut with end of knife

parts.note: to sever is to cut through

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A brutal wound inflicted with the point of a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: severe and harsh both mean stern or extreme.

clue.text: School teacher upset about hours being changed

indicators.note: about means around, one group going round the other
upset means knocked over, so the letters of teacher are scrambled
being changed tells us the letters of hours are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher is annoyed that the timetable has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TEACHER into CHARTE...E, which goes 'about' RHOUS, the letters of HOURS 'being changed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is a well-known English public school in Surrey.

clue.text: Happiest time for those not attending night classes?

definitions.text: Happiest time for those not attending night classes?

parts.words: Happiest time for those not attending night classes?
parts.note: the period of youth often called the happiest of one's life, when lessons happen by day rather than at night

explanation.definitionFit: The years of attending school, proverbially the happiest of one's life.

clue.text: He'll be the first to take over

definitions.text: He'll be the first to take over

parts.words: He'll be the first to take over
parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls; the batsman who starts the innings faces the first

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six deliveries; the batsman opening the innings faces the first ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who goes in first, starting his side's batting.

clue.text: Capital start provided in change round

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
round suggests turning the word change about into a new order

parts.note: to open is to start

explanation.surface: A city's beginning depends on loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges the letters of the money word, and 'in' sends the start word inside them, after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Copenhagen is the capital city of Denmark.

clue.text: Exact payment for something on another's account

definitions.text: Exact payment for something on another's account

parts.words: Exact payment for something on another's account
parts.note: 'exact' is a verb, to demand, and payment is retribution taken on behalf of someone wronged

explanation.definitionFit: To take revenge on behalf of someone who was wronged.

clue.text: Type of whale that comes in for criticism

indicators.note: comes in means the answer is sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A kind of whale is getting a lot of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: The orc is an old name for the killer whale or grampus.

clue.text: Renowned solicitor to open proceedings

parts.note: star as an adjective means renowned or leading
a tout is one who solicits custom

explanation.surface: A famous lawyer begins a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer; here it is someone who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: To start out is to begin, set off on a course.

clue.text: Have to concede

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both possess and admit, as in owning up.

clue.text: Train speed reduced to walking pace

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an adjective meaning slow or on foot

indicators.note: reduced to suggests being broken down into a different form

explanation.surface: A locomotive slows until it is crawling along.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian means going on foot, and so dull and slow-moving.

clue.text: Kick, taking fresh wind into account

parts.note: RE as a prefix means again, afresh
to coil is to wind round

explanation.surface: A gun's jolt is measured while allowing for the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' rhymes with 'kind', not 'pinned'; 'taking' and 'into account' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The kick of a firearm when it is fired is called its recoil.

clue.text: The country's top people emerging from Heathrow?

definitions.text: The country's top people emerging from Heathrow?

parts.words: The country's top people emerging from Heathrow?
parts.note: people coming off a plane have touched down; the country's upper class are the landowning set

explanation.walkthrough: Heathrow is London's main airport, where travellers land.
explanation.definitionFit: The landowning upper class of the British countryside.

clue.text: Called me in and exploded

indicators.note: in shows one word placed inside another
exploded means blown apart, scattering the letters of and

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned me and then lost their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' scatters the little joining word into NAD, and 'in' puts ME inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be named is to be called by a given name.

clue.text: Brave man: he has heart of iron

indicators.note: heart of takes the middle letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A courageous fellow is said to have a core of iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A man admired for courage and noble deeds.

clue.text: Impressive plea for restitution

parts.note: 'impressive' read as to do with printing impressions: a proofreader's request to restore deleted text

explanation.definitionFit: A proofreading mark meaning let it stand, restoring a struck-out word.

clue.text: A pound to one on Britain

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A betting tip offers odds on Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pound to one on' reads like a bookmaker's odds; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient poetic name for Britain or England.

clue.text: Swirling mist hides the way forward

indicators.note: hides means keeps inside, so one piece encloses the other
swirling means stirred round, so the letters of mist move about

parts.note: a mode is a way or method

explanation.surface: A thick fog conceals the road ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swirling' turns the fog word into IMST, and 'hides' holds the way inside it. 'forward' is the adjective meaning bold.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of presumptuous or brazen, lacking modesty.

clue.text: Pay for a seat

definitions.meaning: to ... a bill is to pay it

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means pay up a debt; the noun is a long wooden bench.

clue.text: Tried to construct huge carport

indicators.note: construct means to build, assembling the letters into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to build an enormous garage.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the Michigan city famed as the home of the American car industry.
